regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Vismodegib for advanced basal cell skin cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Vismodegib is used to help control advanced basal cell skin cancer when the source-specific criteria are met. Discuss whether the aim is shrinkage, symptom relief, longer disease control or another agreed goal, and how surgery or radiotherapy has been considered.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00236: symptomatic metastatic basal cell carcinoma, or locally advanced basal cell carcinoma unsuitable for surgery or radiotherapy.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Vismodegib blocks a protein called Smoothened in the Hedgehog signalling pathway. This pathway can drive basal cell cancer growth. Blocking it can also affect normal hair follicles, taste and muscle function, which helps explain hair loss, altered taste and cramps. This treatment is different from a cream applied to a skin lesion.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Take vismodegib once every day at the same time, continuously while the team considers it beneficial and tolerable. A 28-day calendar organises the four-week review; it is not a planned seven-day break or a fixed number of courses.
key_points: The formal pregnancy-prevention programme is essential; restrictions continue after stopping.
A four-week review calendar does not create a routine drug holiday.
Routine CPK testing is not specified by the cited NCCP schedule; muscle symptoms need individual assessment.

supportive_care.premedication_and_prophylaxis: No universal supportive prescription is issued. Review the NCCP emetogenic category and individual local plan.
supportive_care.patient_education: Call urgently for blistering or peeling skin, mouth sores with rash or fever, severe muscle pain or weakness, or dark urine. Seek immediate advice about suspected pregnancy or exposure. Report taste change, reduced eating and weight loss early so support can start.
supportive_care.special_support: Vismodegib can cause severe harm to an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant need the formal pregnancy-prevention programme, including two recommended contraceptive methods (one highly effective method plus a barrier method), unless the agreed alternative is continuous abstinence, during treatment and for 24 months after stopping. Pregnancy tests are supervised before treatment and monthly, even with absent periods. Men must use a condom, with spermicide if available, during sex with a female partner during treatment and for two months afterwards, including after a vasectomy. Report a suspected patient or partner pregnancy immediately. Do not breastfeed or donate blood during treatment or for 24 months afterwards; do not donate semen during treatment or for two months afterwards. Ask the team to explain and document the full programme; this summary does not replace its materials.

monitoring_and_toxicity.baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests; medicine review and pregnancy-prevention programme assessment for women and men. If pregnancy is possible, a supervised pregnancy test is needed within seven days before starting.
monitoring_and_toxicity.before_each_cycle: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every four weeks. Review cramps, strength, taste, eating, weight, hair/skin changes and treatment tolerance. Pregnancy testing is monthly when applicable, even if periods stop.
monitoring_and_toxicity.ongoing: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests every four weeks. Review cramps, strength, taste, eating, weight, hair/skin changes and treatment tolerance. Pregnancy testing is monthly when applicable, even if periods stop.
priority_toxicities: Altered or lost taste and poor appetite
Severe harm to pregnancy; prolonged prevention requirements
monitoring_and_toxicity.urgent_review_signals: Call urgently for blistering or peeling skin, mouth sores with rash or fever, severe muscle pain or weakness, or dark urine. Seek immediate advice about suspected pregnancy or exposure. Report taste change, reduced eating and weight loss early so support can start.
monitoring_and_toxicity.longitudinal_schedule: Agree continuing clinical/skin review, any response imaging and support for ongoing effects. The pregnancy-prevention, donation and breastfeeding restrictions continue after the last dose for their specified periods.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Take vismodegib once every day at the same time, continuously while the team considers it beneficial and tolerable. A 28-day calendar organises the four-week review; it is not a planned seven-day break or a fixed number of courses.
administration.route_and_duration: Swallow the prescribed capsule whole with about 200 mL of water, with or without food, at the same time each day. Do not open, crush or chew it. Keep it in its labelled pack, away from children, and return unused capsules to the pharmacy.
administration.practical_workflow: If a dose is missed, skip it and take the next dose at the usual time. Do not double up. If you vomit after taking it, ask the oncology team or pharmacist before taking more; do not assume that the dose needs replacing.
administration.observation_and_access: Use the prescribed route, appointments, access/handling instructions and local observation policy.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Dabrafenib and trametinib for advanced BRAF-mutated melanoma
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Dabrafenib and trametinib block two points in a growth pathway used by BRAF V600-mutated melanoma. In this advanced-disease setting the aim is disease control, with the effect on symptoms, side effects and your priorities reviewed regularly.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00415a: unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600 mutation. This route covers advanced disease; the separate 00415/adjuvant guide covers the 12-month postoperative setting. Separate 00415b postoperative stage III BRAF V600 setting: planned 12 months, with its own patient route and consent discussion.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: A BRAF V600 change can keep the cell-growth pathway switched on. Dabrafenib blocks the altered BRAF protein. It is paired with a MEK inhibitor to act on the same pathway at another point. The BRAF result comes from tumour testing; it does not automatically mean a hereditary condition. MEK carries growth signals further along the pathway below BRAF. Trametinib blocks MEK alongside dabrafenib. Normal heart, eye, lung and other tissues can also be affected, which is why scheduled tests and prompt symptom reporting matter.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Take dabrafenib twice daily, around 12 hours apart, and trametinib once daily. Both are taken every day unless the team instructs a hold. Treatment for advanced melanoma continues while beneficial and tolerable; there is no preset cycle total. A 28-day calendar is a review period, not a treatment-free week. For the separate adjuvant route, treatment is planned for 12 months; do not transfer the advanced-disease endpoint.
key_points: Advanced and adjuvant treatment are distinct; do not apply a 12-month endpoint to all patients.
Fever holds both drugs; other toxicities may have component-specific rules. The treating team decides restart and dose changes.
The historical PDF contains adjuvant00415b while the reviewed catalogue excerpt lists00415a; current source reconciliation must resolve/record this difference.
The current NCCP document gives different skin-review intervals in two sections; the local team must confirm and record the interval rather than treating one as universally agreed.

supportive_care.premedication_and_prophylaxis: No universal supportive prescription is issued. Review the NCCP emetogenic category and individual local plan.
supportive_care.patient_education: Fever is a particular concern. At 38°C or above, withhold both medicines and contact the oncology team promptly under the written fever plan; recurrent episodes may require action at the first symptoms. Infection and dehydration also need assessment. Restart only when the team tells you. Urgent help is also needed for vision change, severe rash, chest pain, breathlessness, bleeding or severe muscle symptoms.
supportive_care.special_support: Discuss fertility and pregnancy precautions before starting. Use an effective alternative to hormonal contraception during treatment and for two weeks after dabrafenib and 16 weeks after trametinib; dabrafenib can make hormonal contraception less effective. The team must confirm the method and the later applicable end date for the combination. Do not breastfeed during treatment; ask when it is safe to resume. Report a possible pregnancy promptly.

monitoring_and_toxicity.baseline: Confirm the BRAF V600 tumour result and advanced-disease treatment goal. Full blood count, kidney/liver tests, ECG and echocardiogram, skin examination and eye assessment when indicated.
monitoring_and_toxicity.before_each_cycle: Blood count, kidney/liver tests monthly. ECG and echocardiogram at four weeks, then every 12 weeks and after dose modification. Regular skin reviews are required: ask the team to document the interval because the source gives monthly and 60-day instructions in different sections. Head/neck examination every three months and chest CT every six months are specified surveillance checks; disease-response imaging follows the individual plan.
monitoring_and_toxicity.ongoing: Blood count, kidney/liver tests monthly. ECG and echocardiogram at four weeks, then every 12 weeks and after dose modification. Regular skin reviews are required: ask the team to document the interval because the source gives monthly and 60-day instructions in different sections. Head/neck examination every three months and chest CT every six months are specified surveillance checks; disease-response imaging follows the individual plan.
priority_toxicities: Skin rash and new skin tumours
Harm to pregnancy and drug interactions
Bleeding, liver changes and muscle injury
monitoring_and_toxicity.urgent_review_signals: Fever is a particular concern. At 38°C or above, withhold both medicines and contact the oncology team promptly under the written fever plan; recurrent episodes may require action at the first symptoms. Infection and dehydration also need assessment. Restart only when the team tells you. Urgent help is also needed for vision change, severe rash, chest pain, breathlessness, bleeding or severe muscle symptoms.
monitoring_and_toxicity.longitudinal_schedule: Continue skin surveillance for six months after stopping as specified by the regimen, and arrange the ongoing melanoma follow-up plan. Review symptoms, heart/eye concerns and contraception instructions after treatment.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Take dabrafenib twice daily, around 12 hours apart, and trametinib once daily. Both are taken every day unless the team instructs a hold. Treatment for advanced melanoma continues while beneficial and tolerable; there is no preset cycle total. A 28-day calendar is a review period, not a treatment-free week.
administration.route_and_duration: Swallow the prescribed capsules/tablet whole with water. Take each dose at least one hour before food or at least two hours after food. Take the once-daily trametinib dose at the same time each day, alongside either the morning or evening dabrafenib dose according to your written plan. Keep the prescribed storage instructions.
administration.practical_workflow: The missed-dose windows differ: take missed dabrafenib only when more than six hours remain before the next dose; take missed trametinib only when more than 12 hours remain. Otherwise skip it. Do not double up. Do not take an extra trametinib dose after vomiting; contact the team or pharmacist about any vomited or uncertain dose.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Encorafenib and binimetinib for advanced BRAF-mutated melanoma
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Encorafenib and binimetinib block two points in the BRAF-MEK growth pathway to help control eligible advanced melanoma. The team reviews response, symptoms and side effects to decide whether the treatment continues.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00563: adults with advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a BRAF V600 mutation.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Encorafenib blocks the BRAF V600 growth signal in eligible melanoma cells. Binimetinib acts further down the same pathway. They have different dose schedules and different safety decisions, so the prescription for one must not be assumed to apply to the other. Binimetinib inhibits MEK in the cell-growth pathway. It can also affect normal muscle, heart and retinal tissues. CK blood tests, heart checks and prompt reporting of eye or muscle changes help the team identify problems before they become more serious.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Take encorafenib once daily and binimetinib twice daily, around 12 hours apart, continuously unless the team tells you to hold them. Treatment continues while beneficial and tolerable. A 28-day review calendar does not mean a routine break or a fixed total number of cycles.
key_points: Temporary holds may need coordinated changes to both medicines; no patient-led dose adjustment.
The regimen is advanced melanoma; it is not an adjuvant treatment template.
No trial outcome percentage is assigned without confirming the exact population, comparison and follow-up.
Tumour lysis syndrome is a source-listed risk, especially with high tumour burden, kidney problems or dehydration. The team decides whether extra hydration and blood checks are needed.

supportive_care.premedication_and_prophylaxis: No universal supportive prescription is issued. Review the NCCP emetogenic category and individual local plan.
supportive_care.patient_education: Contact the team promptly for new visual symptoms, chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, faintness, severe muscle pain or weakness, dark urine, bleeding, severe rash, persistent diarrhoea or severe abdominal pain. Do not continue one medicine at an unchanged dose if the other has been held without a specific team instruction. Report markedly reduced urine, persistent vomiting, new muscle cramps or weakness, or palpitations promptly; the team may need to check salts, kidney function and tumour lysis risk.
supportive_care.special_support: Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least one month after the last dose. Hormonal contraception needs an additional or alternative barrier method because interactions can reduce effectiveness. Discuss fertility beforehand and follow the team’s breastfeeding instructions. Report a possible pregnancy promptly.

monitoring_and_toxicity.baseline: Confirm BRAF V600 and treatment setting. Full blood count, kidney/liver tests, creatine kinase (CK) and creatinine, blood pressure, ECG, a heart-pumping assessment by echo or MUGA, and skin examination.
monitoring_and_toxicity.before_each_cycle: Blood count, kidney/liver tests monthly. CK and creatinine monthly for the first six months, then as indicated. ECG at four weeks, then every 12 weeks and after dose changes; heart-pumping assessment every three months. Skin assessment every 60 days, head/neck examination every three months and chest CT every six months. Response scans follow the individual plan.
monitoring_and_toxicity.ongoing: Blood count, kidney/liver tests monthly. CK and creatinine monthly for the first six months, then as indicated. ECG at four weeks, then every 12 weeks and after dose changes; heart-pumping assessment every three months. Skin assessment every 60 days, head/neck examination every three months and chest CT every six months. Response scans follow the individual plan.
priority_toxicities: Skin reactions and new skin tumours
Nausea, vomiting, fatigue and joint pain
monitoring_and_toxicity.urgent_review_signals: Contact the team promptly for new visual symptoms, chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, faintness, severe muscle pain or weakness, dark urine, bleeding, severe rash, persistent diarrhoea or severe abdominal pain. Do not continue one medicine at an unchanged dose if the other has been held without a specific team instruction. Report markedly reduced urine, persistent vomiting, new muscle cramps or weakness, or palpitations promptly; the team may need to check salts, kidney function and tumour lysis risk.
monitoring_and_toxicity.longitudinal_schedule: Continue skin surveillance for six months after stopping as specified by the regimen. Agree continuing symptom/organ checks, the next melanoma assessment and medicine-specific pregnancy precautions.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Take encorafenib once daily and binimetinib twice daily, around 12 hours apart, continuously unless the team tells you to hold them. Treatment continues while beneficial and tolerable. A 28-day review calendar does not mean a routine break or a fixed total number of cycles.
administration.route_and_duration: The usual method is to swallow the prescribed capsules/tablets whole with water, with or without food. If swallowing is difficult, ask the pharmacist for the source-permitted preparation: Braftovi capsules may be opened into about 20 mL of apple puree for immediate use, and Mektovi 15 mg tablets may be dispersed in about 10 mL of water, orange juice or apple juice, taken immediately, followed by a further 10 mL rinse. Do not assume this applies to other tablet strengths or improvise a preparation. Keep doses at consistent times. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, and have all medicines and supplements checked.
administration.practical_workflow: For a missed encorafenib dose, take it only if more than 12 hours remain before the next dose. For binimetinib, do not take a missed dose if fewer than six hours remain before the next; ask the pharmacist if timing is uncertain. Do not double doses. If either medicine is vomited, do not take an extra dose; take the next scheduled dose unless the team advises otherwise.
administration.observation_and_access: Use the prescribed route, appointments, access/handling instructions and local observation policy.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Nivolumab and ipilimumab for advanced melanoma
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Nivolumab and ipilimumab help immune cells recognise and attack melanoma. The combination phase is followed by nivolumab alone when appropriate. The aim in this setting is to control advanced disease; benefit and toxicity are reviewed for the individual.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00431a: advanced unresectable or metastatic melanoma in adults. This patient guide is the melanoma context, not the separate liver-cancer indication.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1, a signal that can reduce T-cell activity. This can help immune cells act against melanoma, but it can also allow inflammation in healthy organs. It is not conventional chemotherapy and side effects can occur even after doses have stopped. Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, another checkpoint involved in controlling T cells. Combining it with nivolumab increases immune activity and can increase immune-related toxicity. The four-dose combination phase has a different treatment plan from nivolumab maintenance.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
key_points: This is nivolumab1/ipilimumab3, not the lower-ipilimumab combination.
Four induction doses do not mean the whole treatment course is four doses.
Prior immune toxicity and permanent-stop decisions remain relevant when maintenance starts.
No routine percentage dose reductions: the team may hold or stop immunotherapy and treat the adverse effect.

supportive_care.premedication_and_prophylaxis: No universal supportive prescription is issued. Review the NCCP emetogenic category and individual local plan.
supportive_care.patient_education: Immunotherapy can cause inflammation in healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Contact the oncology team promptly for new diarrhoea, blood in stools, cough or breathlessness, yellow skin or eyes, severe headache, vision changes, marked thirst, unusual weakness or a spreading rash. Tell any clinician that you are receiving or have received immunotherapy.

Use the contraception plan and after-treatment duration specified for the medicines you receive; ask about breastfeeding restrictions. Tell the team promptly about possible pregnancy. monitoring_and_toxicity.urgent_review_signals: Immunotherapy can cause inflammation in healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Contact the oncology team promptly for new diarrhoea, blood in stools, cough or breathlessness, yellow skin or eyes, severe headache, vision changes, marked thirst, unusual weakness or a spreading rash. Tell any clinician that you are receiving or have received immunotherapy.
monitoring_and_toxicity.longitudinal_schedule: Continue to report possible immune effects for at least five months after the last dose, as specified by NCCP, and for longer whenever your team advises. Keep any steroid taper, hormone-replacement plan and relevant follow-up tests. Response imaging follows your individual plan.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: The combination phase gives nivolumab followed by ipilimumab by IV infusion every three weeks for up to four doses. If appropriate, nivolumab alone then continues on the team-selected two-weekly or four-weekly schedule, by the prescribed IV or subcutaneous route. After the last combination dose, the first two-weekly maintenance dose starts three weeks later; the first four-weekly maintenance dose starts six weeks later in this melanoma schedule. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, subject to review.
administration.route_and_duration: At each combination visit, nivolumab is given before ipilimumab, as separate IV infusions. The source schedule gives each over 30 minutes; allow extra time for assessment, preparation and observation. Maintenance may be IV or subcutaneous nivolumab with its own dose and appointment interval. The route and interval are recorded in your plan; they are not interchangeable on your own.
administration.practical_workflow: If an appointment is missed or treatment is held, contact the unit for a new plan. Do not count a missed visit as a dose received. A move to maintenance does not erase previous immune toxicity or a permanent-stop decision.
administration.observation_and_access: Use the prescribed route, appointments, access/handling instructions and local observation policy.

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Cemiplimab for advanced cutaneous squamous cell cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: Cemiplimab helps immune cells act against advanced cutaneous squamous cell cancer when curative surgery or radiotherapy is not suitable. The team reviews cancer control, symptoms, side effects and your priorities to decide whether to continue.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: NCCP 00812b: metastatic or locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma when curative surgery or curative radiotherapy is not appropriate. This guide covers skin SCC, not the separate cervical-cancer indication.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Cemiplimab blocks PD-1 signalling that can limit T-cell activity. This may help the immune system attack cutaneous squamous cell cancer. Increased immune activity can also inflame healthy organs, so new symptoms need attention even if the visible skin tumour appears to improve.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cemiplimab is given by IV infusion on Day 1 every 21 days. The usual source dose is 350 mg over 30 minutes; the prescription and visit checks confirm your treatment. There is no fixed cycle total in this regimen: treatment continues while the team considers it beneficial and tolerable.

supportive_care.special_support: Use effective contraception during cemiplimab treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. Discuss fertility before treatment, and follow the medicine-specific breastfeeding restrictions. Report a possible pregnancy promptly.

monitoring_and_toxicity.baseline: Full blood count, kidney/liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests; hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis B core antibody and hepatitis C testing. Review autoimmune conditions, organ transplantation, previous immune reactions and medicines.
